hypotheses.justification: The statement does not mention it: adeleBddPrincipal, adeleBdd, adeleSpace and globalSub are defined without any HasPrincipalDivisors argument. It is used only in the proof, to get globalSub ≤ adeleSpace (via diagonal_mem_adeleSpace). The equality holds without it, with S = adeleBdd D ≤ C = adeleSpace (adeleBdd_le_adeleSpace, no hypothesis) and T = globalSub arbitrary: S.comap C.subtype ⊔ T.comap C.subtype ≤ (S ⊔ T).comap C.subtype by monotonicity of comap. Conversely, if x ∈ C and x = s + t with s ∈ S, t ∈ T, then t = x - s ∈ C since S ≤ C, so s ∈ S∩C and t ∈ T∩C, and x lies in the sup of the two comaps. A Lean proof pushes forward along the injective C.subtype with map_sup and map_comap_subtype. That reduces it to S ⊔ (T ⊓ C) = (S ⊔ T) ⊓ C, which is the modular law and follows from S ≤ C. The existing helper Submodule.comap_subtype_sup_of_le_of_le assumes T ≤ C, so it would need a variant or direct proof that drops that assumption. I did not check the exact Mathlib name for the modular law.
